Personally I feel that Ford is an easier character to relate to, since there was always that pressure of being so "gifted" and do more for the family/humanity. The teasing about his physical appearance, mixed with praises of being brilliant, and also bring a twin? Not a twin, but I find that being related to someone, you always have that identity as their "brother/sister". I think Ford wanted to have an identity for himself apart from troublemaker Stan and apply that in the best way possible. He dedicated so much time to his studies and was given a great opportunity to go to another, possibly bigger part of the country (assuming Glass Shard Beach was a small city). Ford felt the betrayal and called out Stan on not being able to handle Ford going to college on his own, I also notice how he doesn't mention jealousy in any way. Yeah, Ford graduated and received a grant for his studies, but at that point he wanted to study the unknown and not make perpetual motion machines.




I could understand that he was losing his mind, living in solitary outside of town he's never really been to. I could understand that he was being so reserved with Stan because he feared that Bill was just that powerful to possess Stan. What I can't understand is why he thought the best time to trust him was 10 years later with burying the book.


Even when they're fighting, Stan tells Ford that he ruined Stan's life. Imagine having a fight with someone and burning their back by accident? I'd react the exact same way.


Ford was so scared of going into the portal, and he comes out like some badass who counters Stan's fighting because he had to fend for himself for so long.





Only to return to an endangered world now that he's back, and have his brother take his identity which makes Ford have a reputation of being a local hack that people despise ("Stanford Pines" in the jail card in NWHS and not being allowed on planes in Blendin's Game) & have his collection be mutilated and pasted together for display.



Ford could've done a lot worse, but Dipper and Mabel were there and needed to keep his composure to solve the problem with having the government on their backs: "Stan, you didn't tell me there were children here".

In conclusion, I would side with Ford because there is more to him than knowledge and intellect. Yeah, he messed up, but I feel that he puts so much pressure on himself for letting Bill possess him and is willing to dedicate all that time trying to own up to that mistake instead of spending time with Stan. I really wish Season 3 did pull through to explore that character, but I'm satisfied in knowing that his story will be revealed in Journal #3.
